chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hajjal, from Thalabah, from Ma'mar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

He said: 'All goodness is in the sword, and beneath the sword, and in the shade of the sword.' He said, 'And I heard him saying: 'Indeed, all goodness is tied to the forelocks of the cavalry horses until the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What does the hadith say about the location of all goodness in relation to the sword and horses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the centrality of military readiness in Shia thought, linking the physical instrument of jihad (the sword) with the spiritual reward tied to the cavalry (khayl). It reflects the historical context of early Islamic warfare where mobile cavalry were decisive, reinforcing the concept that active struggle (jihad) is the vessel for divine goodness until the Day of Resurrection.
